Bulletin 489 Termination of Agency Relationships and Maine’s Cancellation Control Acts It has come to the Bureau’s attention that some Maine consumers have recently had their homeowners, renters, or personal auto policies nonrenewed solely because the insurer’s agency relationship with a producer has terminated. This is not a lawful basis for nonrenewal.
Insurers are reminded that in Maine, these lines of business are subject to Cancellation Control Acts that grant policyholders the right to renew their policies unless the insurer can demonstrate a valid reason for nonrenewal. The only permissible reasons for nonrenewal are those specified in the Maine Automobile Insurance Cancellation Control Act1 or the Maine Property Cancellation Control Act,2 as applicable. For all policies that are subject to either Control Act, the reason or reasons for nonrenewal action must be explicitly stated in the notice of nonrenewal. Vague explanations such as “underwriting reasons” are insufficient.3
Producers who no longer represent a particular insurer are free to offer policyholders alternative coverage with a different insurer, but that does not extinguish the policyholders’ right to renew the coverage they have. KATHLEEN M. BARRON
v.
JOHN D. BARRON

John contends that the court erred in distributing marital property because it used information from Kathleen’s 2022 financial statement instead of information from her 2024 financial statement. 1 We agree, vacate the judgment in part, and remand for further proceedings. We also deny Kathleen’s motion for sanctions, which argues that John’s appeal is frivolous.

In 2022, both Kathleen and John filed financial statements as required by M.R. Civ. P. 108(c). On May 15, 2024, prior to the final hearing on May 31, 2024, Kathleen filed an updated financial statement as required by M.R. Civ. P. 108(d)(4). John did not file an updated financial statement. Title 5 License Maintenance Case Title 5 License Maintenance Case Aug 11, 2026 Providers whose license is under a Title 5 review may use your Title 5 notice to extend your enrollment with MaineCare in MIHMS by six months, and for every six months thereafter, until the Title 5 review is resolved. Providers must complete this update by submitting a maintenance case via the Health PAS Online Portal. They can use the Provider Maintenance User Guide for step-by-step instructions. Select the “Title 5 License Extension” from the licensing board drop-down menu and complete the maintenance case as usual. Providers can use the ALMS website to search for your license and must take a screenshot to upload with the maintenance case to show the Title 5 status. Please ensure the "Term Date” is 6 months after the license expiration date. For example, if you submit your Title 5 review and your license ends on January 30, 2026, extend the “Term Date” out to July 30, 2026. As necessary, repeat this process every six months until the license is renewed. Once the license is renewed, submit another case with the new term date of the license. Providers take note of your license expiration dates and plan to submit a maintenance case to update that license information a minimum of 30 days prior to the license expiration date. Be sure to account for this when planning and submitting other maintenance cases. Note: MaineCare will not reimburse providers for services rendered when they fail to renew and update your license within a maintenance case prior to its expiration. For questions about this process, please contact Provider Enrollment at 1 (866) 690-5585 option 2.

Title IV Postsecondary Institutions: Workforce Pell Program Application Now Open

August 12, 2026

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: August 12, 2026

Title IV Postsecondary Institutions: Workforce Pell Program Application Now Open

MAINE- The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) - https://www.maine.gov/swb/board/index.shtml announced the launch of Maine's Workforce Pell Application - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/pages/workforce-pell , providing eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with an online process to seek approval to offer Workforce Pell-eligible programs.

The launch of the application follows the U.S. Department of Education's publication of the final Workforce Pell regulations - https://www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-issues-final-rule-create-new-workforce-pell-grant-program (effective July 20, 2026). Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers. Under Workforce Pell, states are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before approval by the U.S. Department of Education.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state," said Vaughan Woodruff, Chair, State Workforce Development Board. "The Maine Workforce Pell program makes it easier for individuals to access those opportunities, strengthening the futures of Maine workers and Maine's businesses."

On July 30, the SWDB approved the Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/final-workforce-pell-determination-policy-8.11.2026.pdf , establishing the state's process for identifying, reviewing, and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. Developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System, and University of Maine System, the policy is designed to align eligible programs with high-skill, high-wage, in-demand occupations; ensure quality outcomes for students; and provide a transparent and consistent process for institutions and learners.

"Workforce Pell is an important step toward building a stronger workforce and expanding opportunities for people to gain the skills they need to succeed," said Laura Fortman, Commissioner of the Maine Department of Labor. "By aligning short-term training with the skills Maine employers need, these programs will create pathways to good jobs and help businesses find qualified workers. The State Workforce Development Board's clear, transparent process will ensure training prepares people for in-demand careers while meeting the needs of Maine's economy."
